times.label: Before the story
When the favourite vanished and its trainer was murdered

labels.label: When the favourite vanished and its trainer was murdered
When Silver Blaze vanished and John Straker was murdered

times.quote: the singular disappearance of the favourite for the Wessex Cup, and the tragic murder of its trainer
times.note: This is the struggle in the hollow on Monday night (¶19, ¶35–37), after Straker left the house at one and before seven in the morning. Holmes says the horse was frightened by the light and lashed out, and the steel shoe struck Straker on the forehead. As he fell, his own knife gashed his thigh (¶226).

times.label: Tuesday evening
times.quote: On Tuesday evening I received telegrams

times.label: The day before, while Holmes brooded

labels.label: The day before, while Holmes brooded
Wednesday, while Holmes brooded

times.quote: For a whole day my companion had rambled about the room
times.note: Holmes's 'yesterday' (¶14), between Tuesday evening and Thursday morning (¶13). The fresh editions are sent up during this day.

times.label: When Watson read the Telegraph and the Chronicle
times.quote: I have seen what the _Telegraph_ and the _Chronicle_ have to say
times.note: Before the journey; not otherwise dated.

times.label: When Fitzroy Simpson was arrested
times.quote: beyond the arrest of young Fitzroy Simpson nothing had been done
times.note: Gregory arrests him on his arrival (¶39); Simpson's statement and the cravat put to him (¶40). Known to Holmes by Thursday morning.

times.label: One morning, at breakfast

labels.label: One morning, at breakfast
Thursday morning, at breakfast

times.quote: as we sat down together to our breakfast one morning

times.label: Thursday morning, at Paddington
times.quote: which he had procured at Paddington

labels.label: One morning, at Paddington
Thursday morning, at Paddington

times.label: Thursday morning, in the train from Paddington
times.quote: an hour or so later I found myself in the corner of a first-class carriage
times.note: Holmes reads the papers, before Reading.

labels.label: One morning, in the train from Paddington
Thursday morning, in the train from Paddington

times.label: Thursday morning, the train passing Reading
times.quote: We had left Reading far behind us

labels.label: One morning, the train passing Reading
Thursday morning, the train passing Reading

times.label: Thursday morning, in the train well past Reading
times.quote: We had left Reading far behind us before he thrust the last one of them under the seat
times.note: The cigar-case, the speed reckoning (¶8–10) and Holmes's talk of the case (¶10–16).

labels.label: One morning, in the train well past Reading
Thursday morning, in the train well past Reading

times.label: Years before, while Straker served Colonel Ross as jockey and then as trainer
times.quote: He has served the Colonel for five years as jockey and for seven as trainer
times.note: Twelve years of service up to now; Simpson's squandering of his fortune upon the turf (¶39) is also in this long past, undated.

times.label: When Fitzroy Simpson registered his bets against the favourite
times.quote: bets to the amount of five thousand pounds had been registered by him against the favourite
times.note: Before the catastrophe; not otherwise dated.

times.label: When Fitzroy Simpson came down to Dartmoor
times.quote: he had come down to Dartmoor in the hope of getting some information
times.note: Before Monday evening, when he met the maid; not otherwise dated.

times.label: Monday evening, before nine
times.quote: On that evening the horses had been exercised and watered as usual
times.note: ¶19 names the night: 'last Monday night when the catastrophe occurred'.

times.label: Monday evening, nine o'clock
times.quote: the stables were locked up at nine o'clock
times.note: Two lads walk up to the trainer's house for supper in the kitchen; Hunter stays on guard.

times.label: Monday evening, a few minutes after nine, the maid on the path
times.quote: At a few minutes after nine the maid, Edith Baxter, carried down to the stables his supper
times.note: The stranger stops her within thirty yards of the stables (¶21–24).

times.label: Monday evening, the maid and the stranger at the stable window
times.quote: ran past him to the window through which she was accustomed to hand the meals
times.note: The stranger speaks with Hunter through the window (¶26–29); Hunter goes for the dog; the maid flees to the house.

times.label: Monday evening, a minute later, Hunter runs out with the dog
times.quote: A minute later, however, when Hunter rushed out with the hound he was gone
times.note: Hunter locks the door before he leaves it (¶31) and searches round the buildings.

times.label: Monday night, when the other lads returned
times.quote: Hunter waited until his fellow-grooms had returned, when he sent a message to the trainer

times.label: Monday night, when Straker heard Hunter's message
times.quote: Straker was excited at hearing the account

times.label: Monday night, one in the morning, Straker leaves the house
times.quote: Mrs. Straker, waking at one in the morning, found that he was dressing
times.note: Rain pattering against the window; he pulls on his mackintosh and walks out towards the stables.

times.label: When the favourite was taken from his stall
times.quote: the favourite’s stall was empty
times.note: Holmes says Straker went down to the stables in the dead of the night and took out Silver Blaze (¶220). The dog did not bark enough to wake the lads (¶219). The police had held that Simpson took him out (¶46).

times.label: The next morning, at seven
times.quote: Mrs. Straker awoke at seven in the morning
times.note: She finds her husband not returned and goes with the maid to the stables: the door open, Hunter stupefied, the stall empty.

times.label: The next morning, the search from the knoll and the finding of the body
times.quote: on ascending the knoll near the house
times.note: The lads roused, the search, the coat on the furze-bush and the body in the hollow (¶34–35).

labels.label: The next morning, the search from the knoll
The next morning, the search from the knoll and the finding of the body

times.label: When Hunter recovered from his stupor
times.quote: Hunter, on recovering from his stupor

times.label: When the remains of the stable-lad's supper were analysed
times.quote: an analysis has shown that the remains of his supper

times.label: When a reward was offered for the missing horse
times.quote: although a large reward has been offered

times.label: When Inspector Gregory arrived
times.quote: On his arrival he promptly found and arrested the man

times.label: Next Tuesday, at the fall of the flag
times.quote: at the fall of the flag next Tuesday
times.note: The Wessex Cup. Holmes watches the start through Watson's field-glass (¶199).

labels.label: Next Tuesday, at the fall of the flag
Four days later, the start of the Wessex Cup

times.label: When Inspector Gregory examined the stables and out-houses round Tavistock
times.quote: I have also examined every stable and out-house in Tavistock, and for a radius of ten miles
times.note: Before Holmes and Watson arrive; not otherwise dated.

times.label: When Inspector Gregory examined the Mapleton stables
times.quote: We have, however, examined the stables, and there is nothing to connect him with the affair
times.note: Before Holmes and Watson arrive; not ordered against the other searches.

times.label: Tuesday, when the gypsies were gone
times.quote: On Tuesday they were gone
times.note: The gypsies were encamped on Monday night within a mile of the spot of the murder (¶62).

times.label: When the traces of the gypsies' camp were found
times.quote: We have found traces which show that a party of gypsies encamped on Monday night
times.note: Before Holmes and Watson arrive.

times.label: Two summers when Fitzroy Simpson lodged at Tavistock
times.quote: He has twice lodged at Tavistock in the summer
times.note: Before the story; two stays, not otherwise dated.

times.label: When Silas Brown laid his bets upon the Wessex Cup
times.quote: Silas Brown, the trainer, is known to have had large bets upon the event
times.note: Before the race; not otherwise dated.

times.label: When Fitzroy Simpson says he lost his cravat
times.quote: declares that he had lost it
times.note: Simpson's claim only; the maid says the stranger wore it on Monday evening (¶35).

times.label: Thursday evening, at Tavistock station
times.quote: It was evening before we reached the little town of Tavistock
times.note: Colonel Ross and Inspector Gregory meet them in the station (¶47–50).

times.label: Thursday evening, driving in the landau through Tavistock
times.quote: A minute later we were all seated in a comfortable landau, and were rattling through the quaint old Devonshire city
times.note: Gregory's talk of the case with Holmes (¶51–68); the moor is being scoured for the gypsies at this time (¶64).

times.label: Thursday evening, the landau pulls up at a red-brick villa

labels.label: Thursday evening, the landau pulls up at a red-brick villa
Thursday evening, the landau pulls up at Straker's villa

times.quote: A few minutes later our driver pulled up at a neat little red-brick villa
times.note: Holmes sits on in the carriage, absorbed, until Watson touches his arm (¶69–70). The talk with Gregory and the Colonel at the door follows (¶71–77).

times.label: Thursday evening, Straker's pocket things laid out in the sitting-room
times.quote: We all filed into the front room and sat round the central table
times.note: Gregory opens the tin box. The knife, the papers and the milliner's account are examined (¶78–85).

times.label: Thursday evening, Mrs. Straker in the passage
times.quote: As we emerged from the sitting-room a woman, who had been waiting in the passage
times.note: Holmes asks about the garden-party at Plymouth (¶86–92).

labels.label: Thursday evening, a woman in the passage
Thursday evening, Mrs. Straker in the passage

times.label: The next day, the inquest
times.quote: The inquest is to-morrow

times.label: When Straker's body was brought back to his house
times.quote: Yes; he lies upstairs
times.note: Holmes's 'Straker was brought back here, I presume?' (¶72). Not otherwise dated. The things from his pockets go into Gregory's tin box at some time after the body was found.

times.label: When Mrs. Straker told the Inspector of the knife and of Derbyshire
times.quote: His wife tells us that the knife had lain upon the dressing-table
times.note: Also told in ¶84: 'Mrs. Straker tells us that Derbyshire was a friend of her husband's'. This was before Holmes arrived; it is not otherwise dated.

labels.label: When Mrs. Straker told the Inspector of the knife
When Mrs. Straker told the Inspector of the knife and of Derbyshire

times.label: The times when letters for William Derbyshire were addressed to Straker's house
times.quote: occasionally his letters were addressed here
times.note: This is what Mrs. Straker says. It is undated and in the past.

times.label: When Madame Lesurier made out the account to William Derbyshire
times.quote: a milliner’s account for thirty-seven pounds fifteen made out by Madame Lesurier, of Bond Street, to William Derbyshire
times.note: The text does not date it. The account was in Straker's pocket at his death, so it comes before the crime, but the text does not order it against that point.

times.label: Some little time ago, a garden-party in Plymouth
times.quote: Surely I met you in Plymouth at a garden-party some little time ago
times.note: This is Holmes's claim, and Mrs. Straker denies it (¶90). The dove-coloured silk costume belongs to this claim (¶91–92).

times.label: Thursday evening, the short walk across the moor to the hollow
times.quote: A short walk across the moor took us to the hollow in which the body had been found
times.note: Holmes follows the Inspector outside from Straker's house.

times.label: Thursday evening, at the hollow where the body was found
times.quote: At the brink of it was the furze-bush upon which the coat had been hung
times.note: Talk of the wind, the coat and the matting. Holmes studies the mud, finds the vesta and compares the boots (¶94–108). The Colonel looks at his watch and asks about the entries (¶110–112).

times.label: When the overcoat was laid across the furze-bush
times.quote: Yes, it was laid across the bush
times.note: Holmes says Straker had taken off his overcoat, in spite of the rain, in order to do his delicate task (¶226). There was no wind but very heavy rain (¶94–95). The coat was later seen from the knoll (¶35).

times.label: When the half-burned wax vesta came into the mud of the hollow
times.quote: It was a wax vesta half burned
times.note: Holmes says Straker got behind the horse and struck a light just before the horse lashed out (¶226). The Colonel says this is why he struck the match (¶224).

times.label: When Silver Blaze cast the horseshoe in the Inspector's bag
times.quote: a cast horseshoe of Silver Blaze
times.note: The text does not date it.

times.label: Since Monday night, the feet trampling the ground at the hollow
times.quote: No doubt many feet have been here since Monday night
times.note: This is when the matting was laid at the side and stood upon (¶99). It comes before Holmes arrives at the hollow.

times.label: When the Inspector examined the ground a hundred yards round the hollow
times.quote: I have examined the ground very carefully for a hundred yards in each direction
times.note: This was before Holmes arrived. The boot, the shoe and the horseshoe went into the Inspector's bag at some time before this scene (¶101).

times.label: Thursday evening, before dark, Holmes's walk over the moor
times.quote: I should like to take a little walk over the moor before it grows dark
times.note: Holmes and Watson walk slowly across the moor as the sun sinks behind the Mapleton stables. Holmes reasons out where the horse has gone (¶113–116).

times.label: Thursday evening, the Colonel and the Inspector back at Straker's house
times.quote: You will find us at poor Straker's house when you have finished your walk
times.note: The Colonel asks the Inspector to come back with him (¶110).

times.label: Thursday evening, the drive together into Tavistock
times.quote: we can drive together into Tavistock
times.note: This was planned at ¶112. It begins at ¶175 with 'Drive on, coachman!', after the talk with the stable-lad.

times.label: The next day, when Holmes means to know his ground
times.quote: that I may know my ground to-morrow
times.note: This is the same day as the inquest (¶73), but the text does not order the two.

times.label: Thursday evening, at the long hollow towards Mapleton
times.quote: a few more minutes brought us to the hollow in question
times.note: Holmes finds the horse's track and fits the horseshoe to it.

times.label: Thursday evening, picking up the tracks again close to Mapleton
times.quote: only to pick them up once more quite close to Mapleton
times.note: They cross the marshy bottom and the dry turf, and lose the tracks for half a mile. Here a man's track appears beside the horse's.

times.label: Thursday evening, following the double track towards King's Pyland
times.quote: we both followed along after it
times.note: Watson sees the same tracks coming back in the opposite direction.

times.label: Thursday evening, following the return track
times.quote: Let us follow the return track

times.label: Thursday evening, at the gates of the Mapleton stables
times.quote: It ended at the paving of asphalt which led up to the gates of the Mapleton stables
times.note: The groom runs out. Silas Brown comes out and Holmes whispers to him (¶124–135).

times.label: Thursday evening, Holmes and Silas Brown in the parlour
times.quote: Now, Mr. Brown, I am quite at your disposal
times.note: About twenty minutes (¶137). Watson waits outside.

times.label: Thursday evening, at dusk, Holmes and Silas Brown reappear
times.quote: It was twenty minutes, and the reds had all faded into greys before Holmes and the trainer reappeared
times.note: Brown promises Holmes his instructions will be done (¶138–143).

times.label: Thursday evening, setting off for King's Pyland
times.quote: we set off for King’s Pyland

times.label: Five o'clock the next morning, when Holmes speaks of calling on Silas Brown
times.quote: if I were to call at five o’clock to-morrow morning
times.note: Holmes puts this to the groom as a question. The text does not order it against the inquest or Holmes's study of his ground.

times.label: The next day, when Silas Brown shall hear from Holmes
times.quote: you shall hear from me to-morrow
times.note: Holmes also says 'I shall write to you about it' (¶141).

times.label: When what Silas Brown promises shall be there
times.quote: It shall be there
times.note: This is promised and not dated. The text does not say what it is or where.

times.label: When the horse's track was made in the long hollow
times.quote: The track of a horse was plainly outlined in the soft earth
times.note: The text does not date it. Holmes supposes the horse crossed there after the tragedy, when the hollow 'must have been very wet on Monday night' (¶116). The horseshoe fits the print.

times.label: When a man's track came beside the horse's near Mapleton
times.quote: A man’s track was visible beside the horse’s
times.note: The horse was alone before this point along the trail (¶120–121).

times.label: When the double track turned off towards King's Pyland
times.quote: The double track turned sharp off and took the direction of King’s Pyland

times.label: When the same tracks came back to the Mapleton gates
times.quote: the same tracks coming back again in the opposite direction
times.note: The return track ends at the asphalt paving to the Mapleton gates (¶124).

labels.label: When the same tracks came back the other way
When the same tracks came back to the Mapleton gates

times.label: Thursday evening, trudging back towards King's Pyland
times.quote: remarked Holmes as we trudged along together
times.note: Holmes speaks of Silas Brown and the horse, and says they go back to London by the night train (¶144–156). Watson can draw nothing more from him until they reach the trainer's house (¶157).

times.label: That morning, when Silas Brown, first down, saw a strange horse wandering over the moor
times.quote: when according to his custom he was the first down, he perceived a strange horse wandering over the moor
times.note: This is Holmes's account of what he described to Brown. He calls it 'that morning', and a reader takes it to be the morning after the night of the crime. Brown goes out to the horse and recognises the white forehead.

times.label: That morning, when Silas Brown first set out to lead the horse back to King's Pyland
times.quote: his first impulse had been to lead him back to King’s Pyland
times.note: This is Holmes's account. It matches the double track turning off towards King's Pyland (¶122).

times.label: That morning, when Silas Brown led the horse back and hid it at Mapleton
times.quote: how he had led it back and concealed it at Mapleton
times.note: This is Holmes's account. It matches the return track to the Mapleton gates (¶122–124). Brown means to hide the horse until the race is over (t.race). Watson's 'But his stables had been searched?' (¶147) implies the horse was there when the stables were searched (t.gregory_mapleton). The text does not order the two points strictly.

times.label: Thursday evening, back at the trainer's house, in the parlour
times.quote: until we were back at the trainer’s house. The Colonel and the Inspector were awaiting us in the parlour
times.note: Holmes announces the night-express, asks for the photograph and goes out to question the maid. The Colonel speaks to Watson while Holmes is away, and then Holmes comes back (¶158–168).

times.label: Thursday evening, Holmes out of the room to question the maid
times.quote: I have a question which I should like to put to the maid
times.note: Holmes returns at ¶167.

times.label: Thursday evening, stepping into the carriage, Holmes asks the stable-lad about the sheep
times.quote: As we stepped into the carriage one of the stable-lads held the door open for us
times.note: The talk with Gregory about the dog in the night-time follows as they drive off (¶175–182).

labels.label: Thursday evening, stepping into the carriage, Holmes turns to a stable-lad
Thursday evening, stepping into the carriage, Holmes asks the stable-lad about the sheep

times.label: Of late, when three of the sheep in the paddock went lame
times.quote: three of them have gone lame, sir
times.note: The lad says it was 'of late' (¶172). The text gives no other date.

times.label: In the night-time, when the dog did nothing
times.quote: The dog did nothing in the night-time
times.note: This is the night of the crime, when the horse was fetched out of the stable and the dog did not bark enough to wake the two lads (¶219).

times.label: Thursday night, the night train back to London
times.quote: we both go back to London by the night train
times.note: This is planned. ¶158 calls it 'the night-express'.

times.label: The twenty years Colonel Ross has been on the turf
times.quote: I have been on the turf for twenty years
times.note: The Colonel's own claim; it runs up to the day of the race.

times.label: When the favourite was sent over to the race just as Holmes found him
times.quote: took the liberty of running him just as he was sent over
times.note: Holmes says he found the horse 'in the hands of a faker'. This links back to Brown's 'Should I change it first or not?' (¶140). The text does not date it, but it comes before the race.

times.label: When Colonel Ross scratched his other horse
times.quote: We scratched our other one, and put all hopes on your word
times.note: This was done on Holmes's word that the horse would start (¶161). It comes before the race and is not otherwise dated.

times.label: The day before the race, the betting at fifteen to one
times.quote: You could have got fifteen to one yesterday
times.note: After this the price shortens until it is under three to one on the race day.

times.label: Four days later, in the train to Winchester
times.quote: Four days later Holmes and I were again in the train, bound for Winchester

times.label: Four days later, Colonel Ross meets them outside the station at Winchester
times.quote: Colonel Ross met us by appointment outside the station

times.label: Four days later, driving in the Colonel's drag to the course
times.quote: we drove in his drag to the course beyond the town
times.note: The talk of the horse and the betting (¶184–189).

times.label: Four days later, the drag draws up in the enclosure near the grand stand
times.quote: As the drag drew up in the enclosure near the grand stand
times.note: Watson reads the card. The ring's cries and the numbers go up (¶190–196).

times.label: Four days later, a bay horse in the Colonel's colours canters past
times.quote: a powerful bay horse swept out from the weighing enclosure and cantered past us

times.label: Four days later, the horses come up the straight and pass the post
times.quote: passed the post a good six lengths before its rival

times.label: Four days later, in the weighing enclosure with the winner
times.quote: as we made our way into the weighing enclosure
times.note: Holmes says the horse is the favourite and names the horse as Straker's killer (¶202–214).

times.label: Four days later, the bell for the next race
times.quote: there goes the bell

times.label: A more fitting time, for Holmes's full explanation
times.quote: I shall defer a lengthy explanation until a more fitting time
times.note: This was planned at ¶214. It comes about in the Pullman car that evening (t.pullman, ¶215). The next race, on which Holmes has a bet, comes in between.

times.label: The evening of the race, in a Pullman car back to London
times.quote: We had the corner of a Pullman car to ourselves that evening as we whirled back to London
times.note: Holmes tells Colonel Ross and Watson what happened on the Monday night and how he worked it out (¶215–231). This is the 'more fitting time' he promised (¶214).

times.label: Monday, when curried mutton was chosen for supper at the trainer's house
times.quote: the only two people who could have chosen curried mutton for supper that night
times.note: Holmes's reasoning. Only Straker or his wife could have chosen the dish.

times.label: Monday evening, when the stable-lad's dish was set aside
times.quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy

times.label: Monday evening, when the opium was added to the stable-lad's dish
times.quote: The opium was added after the dish was set aside for the stable-boy
times.note: This comes before the maid carries the supper down. Holmes asks who had access to the dish without the maid seeing them.

times.label: Monday evening, the same dish eaten at the house
times.quote: for the others had the same for supper with no ill effects

times.label: Monday evening, when Fitzroy Simpson dropped his cravat in his flight
times.quote: Simpson in his flight had dropped his cravat
times.note: Holmes's account. This contradicts Simpson's claim that he had lost it (t.simpson_lost_cravat).

times.label: Monday night, when Straker picked up the cravat
times.quote: Straker had picked it up
times.note: Holmes says 'perhaps' it was to secure the horse's leg. The text does not say where or exactly when Straker picked it up.

times.label: Monday night, Straker leads the horse out to the hollow
times.quote: Straker had led out the horse to a hollow where his light would be invisible

times.label: Monday night, when the horse bolted
times.quote: Ah, it bolted, and was cared for by one of your neighbours

times.label: Before the crime, when Straker practised the tendon-nicking on the sheep
times.quote: so astute a man as Straker would not undertake this delicate tendon-nicking without a little practice
times.note: Holmes's surmise, which he says the lad's answer confirmed. This is what lamed the three sheep.

times.label: Cases before now, when trainers laid against their own horses and stopped them by fraud
times.quote: There have been cases before now where trainers have made sure of great sums of money by laying against their own horses
times.note: This is a general past and is not dated.

times.label: The time when Straker led a double life as Derbyshire, with a second establishment
times.quote: Straker was leading a double life, and keeping a second establishment
times.note: The milliner knew him as an excellent customer named Derbyshire, with a very dashing wife (¶229). Holmes believes she plunged him into debt. This period takes in the milliner's account (t.milliner_account) and the letters addressed to Derbyshire (t.derbyshire_letters).

times.label: When Holmes, back in London, called upon the milliner
times.quote: When I returned to London I called upon the milliner
times.note: Holmes takes Straker's photograph with him (¶225). The text does not order this against the train to Winchester.

times.label: The evening of the race, passing Clapham Junction
times.quote: This is Clapham Junction, if I am not mistaken

times.label: The evening of the race, at Victoria, in less than ten minutes
times.quote: we shall be in Victoria in less than ten minutes
times.note: This is expected.

times.label: The evening of the race, a cigar in Holmes and Watson's rooms
times.quote: If you care to smoke a cigar in our rooms, Colonel
times.note: Holmes offers this to the Colonel.

times.label: When the witnesses' statements were taken
times.quote: The girl has sworn
times.note: The sworn and other statements to the police; not otherwise dated.
